newsitem.title: UGANDA: Zaire rebels kill Ugandan rebel chief, report.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels kill Ugandan rebel chief, report.

text.p: Zairean rebels killed a Ugandan rebel leader when he fled wounded into northeast Zaire after an attack on his base in southern Sudan, the Monitor newspaper said on Saturday.
The independent daily said Colonel Juma Oris, leader of the rebel West Nile Bank Front (WNBF) and a former minister under Ugandan dictator Idi Amin, was buried in Kitambala, northeastern Zaire.
Ugandan military sources said last weekend that Oris had been killed in a clash between Ugandan troops and the WNBF near the Ugandan-Sudanese border. The body however was not recovered.
But the Monitor, in a report from Kimba in south Sudan, said Oris and his operations commander, Adinan "Ninja", were wounded when Sudanese rebels destroyed their headquarters in Kimba.

It said Oris, on a stretcher, his wife and two children escaped to neighbouring northeastern Zaire where the rebel leader and two aides were killed by rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL).
The newspaper gave no exact date for the killings.
It said his wife and children were being held by the AFDL.
The Monitor quoted Madut Caesar, a commander with the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), as saying his forces had flattened the WNBF base in Kimba with a barrage of mortar bombs.

"We met some resistance but hit the camp with 100 mm and 130 mm mortars," he said. If the report was true, the death of Oris and destruction of the WNBF base would appear to be a devastating blow to the movement.
Khartoum has accused Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni of arming the SPLA, the largest Sudanese rebel group. It launched offensives in eastern Sudan in January and in the south this month.
Khartoum accuses Uganda, Eritrea and Ethiopia of sending troops into Sudan to fight alongside the rebels since January.
The Zairean government charges that Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi have sent their troops into eastern Zaire in support of the AFDL rebels. All three countries have denied any role.

Oris received military training in Pakistan when he served in the Ugandan army in the 1960s. He was a close associate of Amin, who was overthrown in 1979, and served as minister of lands, minister of information and minister of foreign affairs.
With Amin's fall, Oris fled into exile in Sudan. He formed the WNBF in 1993 with the aim of overthrowing Museveni. He was reputed to have the support of Amin, who now lives in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
